title: Pork with vegetables without carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of lean pork sautéed with a variety of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes, and tomato‑based sauce. The combination of tender meat and mildly sweet vegetables provides a balanced flavor and nutritional profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is a good source of high‑quality protein and B‑vitamins.
Omitting tomato sauce reduces acidity, making the dish gentler on sensitive stomachs.
Vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, and cauliflower retain most of their vitamins when quickly stir‑fried.
The recipe can be easily adapted to different cuisines by changing herbs and spices.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork supplies essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat provides thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Pork and the vegetables contribute iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Excluding potatoes and tomato sauce makes the dish suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Antioxidant vegetables
items.content: Bell pepper and cauliflower contain vitamin C and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Processed meat concerns
items.content: Frequent consumption of pork, especially fatty cuts, may increase cardiovascular risk if lean portions are not chosen.

items.title: Vegetable allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to bell pepper or zucchini.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding salt or pre‑made seasonings can raise sodium levels, which is undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut lean pork into bite‑size cubes and sauté over medium heat until golden. Add diced bell pepper, zucchini, and cauliflower and stir‑fry for 5‑7 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, paprika, and fresh herbs to taste. Serve hot.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
